title: Imprints of dynamical phases in semiclassical entanglement entropy in 2D CFT
authors: Parijat Dey, Semanti Dutta, Bobby Ezhuthachan
abstract: We study the time evolution of semiclassical entanglement entropy in a class of $sl(2,\mathbb{R})$ driven states in a large $c$ conformal field theory (CFT) in $1+1$ spacetime dimensions. Upon varying the parameters of the drive, we find that the entanglement entropy exhibits the signature of the dynamical phases of the driven CFT. We further study the holographic dual of this CFT where the excited states of a minimally coupled scalar in $AdS_3$ induce a backreaction that modifies the background geometry. We compute the back reacted geometry by solving Einstein's equation with the expectation value of the stress tensor in the coherent state as the source term. Subsequently, we calculate the time evolution of the perturbed minimal area and the bulk entanglement entropy at $O(G_N^0)$, up to the sub-leading order in short distance approximation. These results match the CFT entanglement entropy in the boundary at $O(c^0)$, and serve as a nontrivial check of the Faulkner-Lewkowycz-Maldacena (FLM) conjecture for the first quantum correction of holographic entanglement entropy. The details of the check has been provided in the accompanying ancillary notebook.
summary: This work analyzes the time evolution of entanglement entropy in a 2D CFT subjected to periodic driving, revealing distinct dynamical phases. By comparing these results with calculations on the holographic dual ($	ext{AdS}_3$), the authors provide strong evidence supporting the Faulkner-Lewkowycz-Maldacena conjecture for quantum corrections to entanglement entropy.
main_problem: The study investigates how semiclassical entanglement entropy (EE) evolves over time in driven quantum field theories, specifically looking for signatures of underlying dynamical phases.
main_result: The computed bulk entanglement entropy successfully matches the CFT entanglement entropy at leading order, providing a non-trivial verification of the Faulkner-Lewkowycz-Maldacena (FLM) conjecture for first quantum corrections.
method: The authors employ both boundary CFT calculations using the replica method and holographic methods involving solving Einstein's equations to find backreacted geometries and calculating minimal areas.
model_or_system: The system is a 2D Conformal Field Theory (CFT) in $1+1$ dimensions, driven by $	ext{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})$ parameters. Its gravitational dual is Anti-de Sitter space ($	ext{AdS}_3$).

important_parameters: Drive parameters ($\alpha,  eta$), stroboscopic time ($nT$), and the gravitational coupling constant ($G_N$).
main_assumptions: The bulk computation is restricted to small backreaction and short distance approximations; calculations are performed up to specific orders in $c$ or $G_N$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the CFT geometry on a cylinder, plot the total entanglement entropy ($	ext{S}_{	ext{tot}}$) versus time for different dynamical phases (Heating/Non-heating), and show cross-sections of the $	ext{AdS}_3$ bulk.
paper_structure: The paper systematically derives the effective Hamiltonian governing the stroboscopic dynamics, calculates the EE in the CFT using replica methods across three distinct dynamic regimes, and then performs a detailed holographic calculation matching these results by solving Einstein's equations for metric perturbations.
why_interesting: The connection between dynamical phases observed in quantum field theory dynamics (like those driven by Floquet Hamiltonians) and geometric properties derived from gravity (via the FLM conjecture) is highly relevant to understanding non-equilibrium quantum systems.
